bull_bear.body: Rs 1,400 cr organic capex weighted to cables & wires + R&D; strategic renewables investment (Goldi) for supply-chain control; sustained brand investment (A&P ~2.7% of revenue) treated as long-term capital. Distribution-policy reset toward sell-out to improve channel return-on-capital. No buyback/dividend commentary on the call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Market-share erosion:** analysts repeatedly flagged Havells lagging peers in wires & cables (competitor posted high-single-digit wire / mid-single-digit cable growth; Havells ~flat) and continued AC share loss — management deflected to "sell-out reset" and long-term view.
- **Switchgear demand/geopolitics:** West Asia export disruption + trade confusion; recovery hinges on shipping normalization.
- **A&P drag persistence:** elevated Lloyd A&P for "a couple of years" caps near-term Lloyd profitability.
- **RM volatility:** copper/aluminium swings create sell-in timing distortions (dealers destock when prices fall).
- **Channel inventory** lower than normal at quarter-end for cables + ACs — could aid or distort Q2 optics.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Chairman Anil Rai Gupta was confident but notably guarded — repeatedly declined guidance ("we do not give guidance for the year"), brushed off a pointed repeat question on cables/wires share loss ("I don't need to repeat my answer"), and gave a terse "I'm always confident about Havells growth." Defends the aggressive A&P timing on first-principles (long-term brand vs short-term RM noise). CFO Rajiv Goel more forthcoming on specifics (A&P at ~2.7% of revenue, capex split, renewables margin mix). Tone: long-term-oriented, disciplined on pricing, but light on hard numbers and slightly defensive on competitive share.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The profit dip is self-inflicted and deliberate** — a >2x A&P front-load (Rs 286 cr), not a demand problem; the swing factor for the rest of FY27 is A&P normalization, not top line.
- **Switchgear is the quiet worry** — it's the highest-margin segment and lost 260 bps + 4% sales; a sustained West Asia disruption matters more to profit than the volume-flat cables optics.
- **"Sell-out" distribution reset** is the recurring explanation for soft primary volumes (Havells + Lloyd both) — aligning primary to secondary should stabilize but is masking reported growth now.
- **Renewables separation is a signaling move** — management wants investors to track a business it believes "can become very big," but repeatedly refused to size it ("too early").
- Cables capacity is up yet volumes are flat — the market is watching whether the Rs 800 cr build converts, or share continues leaking to peers.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividends paid of Rs 376 crores in Q1 FY27 and Rs 627 crores in FY26 — the dominant financing outflow in both periods.
- Debt-light balance sheet: total non-current liabilities of Rs 675 crores consist of lease liabilities Rs 174 crores, deferred tax Rs 435 crores and other Rs 65 crores, against Total equity of Rs 9,446 crores; ROCE is defined by the company as PBT TTM / Average Capital Employed TTM (Net Worth + Debt) at 23.5%.
- Cash & Cash Equivalent at end of Q1 FY27 of Rs 1,497 crores (deck notes this "also includes bank deposits"), down from Rs 2,351 crores at the beginning of the quarter and Rs 3,353 crores at the start of FY26.
- Operating Net Cash Flow was negative Rs 186 crores in Q1 FY27 (against a positive Rs 1,557 crores for FY26), driven by a Rs 636 crores change in operating assets and liabilities.
- Returns as reported by the company: ROE 18.1% (Q1 FY27) versus 17.6% (Q1 FY26), ROCE 23.5% versus 23.7%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified, multi-brand portfolio (Havells, Lloyd, Havells Crabtree, Standard, REO, Havells Studio) across 24 product verticals reduces reliance on any single category
- In-house manufacturing across 17 national units is viewed by the company as providing a sustainable competitive advantage through differentiation and quality control
- Wide distribution reach: ~20,700 dealers and ~2.72 lakh retailers across India, plus presence in over 70 countries
- Sustained R&D investment (consistently over 1% of revenue) and an 856-strong R&D team supporting a pipeline of patents and new product designs
- Strong balance sheet with zero debt and a healthy cash position; long-term credit rating of AAA and short-term A1+ from CARE
- Premiumisation-led brand building (e.g. Apogee switches range, IPL co-sponsorship) reinforcing brand salience across price points
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global trade volatility and geopolitical uncertainty — FY 2025-26 was marked by US reciprocal tariff actions on several countries (including India) and the outbreak of conflict in West Asia, creating uncertainty around sourcing, logistics, demand patterns and cost structures.
- Commodity price volatility in copper and aluminium — The Cables segment, which is Havells' largest by revenue, witnessed pronounced volatility in key input commodities (copper and aluminium), leading to pricing uncertainties across the market.
- Input cost volatility in Switchgear (BCP) — The Building Circuit Protection segment navigated a challenging environment characterised by input cost volatility and softer demand across retail and project segments.
- Structural LED price deflation in Lighting — FY 2025-26 continued to be another year with LED price deflation in the lighting industry, a multi-year structural headwind weighing on segment revenue and margins despite innovation efforts.
- US tariff exposure on cable exports — Export performance in Cables was impacted during the year due to uncertainties surrounding evolving tariff structures, particularly in the United States.
- Rupee depreciation and elevated inflation impacting consumer demand — Rising commodity prices and a weakening Indian rupee kept inflation elevated during the year, impacting household disposable income and consumer demand for the Company's products.
- Seasonality and weather-dependence of consumer/cooling categories — A subdued/weak summer impacted sales in certain consumer categories during the year, illustrating the Company's exposure to weather-driven demand volatility in cooling and consumer segments.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Switchgear (highest margin):** −4% YoY, −260 bps margin; ~15% international, disrupted by West Asia (no vessels) + RM volatility causing trade destocking; normalized contribution margin 37–40%; Q2 rebound expected.
- **Cables & Wires:** volume ~flat despite added capacity; management attributes to copper/aluminium volatility + a deliberate shift from "sell-in" to "sell-out" (secondary-aligned) distribution; Rs 800 cr of FY27 capex here; capacity utilization "high" but not disclosed.
- **Lloyd (ACs):** single-digit volume, higher value; delayed summer onset + BEE-rating-driven channel destock in prior quarters; contribution margin high-single-digit, targeting double-digit; A&P-heavy (top-of-mind + premiumization).
- **ECD / Lighting:** ECD absorbed price hikes; Lighting ASP stabilized, volume growth resuming, possible price hikes ahead (electronics).
- **Renewables (new segment):** scaling rapidly; Goldi Solar = strategic module supply ("strategic insourcing"); inverters in-house; panels lower-margin than inverters; focus on residential + C&I (not utility scale).

outlook.body:
- **Revenue/margin:** **no annual guidance** (long-standing policy). Qualitative: "healthy outlook on margins," expects demand to improve, contribution margins to stabilize at normalized levels; declined to commit on EBITDA margin.
- **A&P:** normalizes over the full year to **~2.7% of revenue** (Rajiv Goel); Q1 front-loading unwinds; Lloyd A&P stays elevated for "the next couple of years" (premiumization).
- **Capex FY27:** **~Rs 1,400 cr** — ~Rs 800 cr cables & wires, ~Rs 200 cr new R&D centre, remainder across other businesses.
- **Switchgear:** expects a **rebound in Q2** (international + overall) as West Asia shipping normalizes; domestic stable.
- **Lloyd contribution margin:** back to **double digits "sooner than later"** (ex the seasonally weak Q2/Q3).
- **Renewables:** margin improvement expected in **H2** (as consumer-side / inverter mix rises vs low-margin panels); no size target ("too early").

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Portfolio premiumisation across categories (switchgear distribution boards, switches, fans, kitchen appliances) through differentiated, higher-value product launches
- Deepening channel engagement and distribution reach via general trade, modern format retail, e-commerce/quick commerce, and expansion into semi-urban and rural markets
- Reducing import dependency through supplier diversification, dual-sourcing and domestic tie-ups, aligned with 'Make in India'
- In-house manufacturing and backward integration viewed as a source of differentiation and premiumisation, particularly for Lloyd (air conditioners, washing machines, refrigerators, televisions) and cables (Alwar, Tumakuru)
- Expanding Lloyd from an air-conditioner-led brand into a comprehensive home-appliances brand across washing machines, refrigerators and televisions to reduce seasonality dependence
- Entry into adjacent categories leveraging existing engineering strengths — Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE/EV chargers) built on switchgear, protection devices and cables capabilities
- Scaling the renewables business (rooftop solar, solar pumps) with a strategic investment in Goldi Solar to secure panel/module supply and planned backward integration into domestic solar cell manufacturing
- R&D-led innovation and premiumisation (e.g. CRAFT kitchen appliance series, Apogee premium switches range, high-efficiency professional luminaires) to sustain brand differentiation
- Diversified geographic, channel and product-category strategy adopted deliberately to balance revenue concentration and seasonality-led volatility
- For FY 2025-26, Havells confirmed payment of an already-paid Interim Dividend of Rs 4.00 per equity share and proposed a Final Dividend of Rs 6.00 per equity share (face value Rs 1 each) for shareholder approval, indicating a policy of returning cash to shareholders through a mix of interim and final dividends alongside continued reinvestment in capacity expansion. The Statutory Auditors (Price Waterhouse & Co Chartered Accountants LLP) were proposed for re-appointment for a second consecutive five-year term, reflecting continuity in audit oversight as part of the governance framework.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Lloyd commissioned a new refrigerator manufacturing plant at Ghiloth, Rajasthan in March 2026, ahead of schedule, capable of producing Direct Cool, Frost Free, Bottom Mount and Multi-door refrigerators; the plant is IoT 4.0/MES-enabled and co-located with Ghiloth's existing air-conditioner and washing-machine manufacturing, creating an integrated multi-product appliances campus. In Cables, Havells has been accelerating capacity investment: a greenfield plant at Tumakuru was commissioned in September 2024, and further expansions are underway at both the Alwar and Tumakuru locations for domestic and export markets; during FY 2025-26 the company additionally acquired 1,58,200 square metres of land adjacent to the existing Alwar facility to support planned capacity enhancement there. Havells has invested over Rs 700 crores in Cables capacity expansion over the last two years, with further capex planned for FY 2026-27. Manufacturing capability in power cables currently extends up to 132 kV, with the company progressing towards 220 kV and higher extra-high-voltage (EHV) cables, and moving towards adoption of E-Beam (electron beam) technology to expand into railways, defence, EV charging infrastructure and data-centre cable segments; associated investments include EHV testing facilities, automation and quality laboratories. In Switches, Havells commissioned a state-of-the-art in-house paint shop at its Baddi facility during FY 2025-26. Lloyd also announced a new manufacturing line for fully automatic front-load washing machines, with the capacity expected to become operational by December 2026. Separately, Havells acquired a letter of intent from YEIDA for 50 acres of land near the new Noida International Airport, intended for future capacity expansion in consumer goods and home appliances manufacturing.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Infrastructure- and industrial-led demand segments showed strong growth momentum during FY 2025-26 even as consumer categories were impacted by a subdued summer
- GST reduction and a favourable festive season provided demand impetus to select categories
- Sustained real estate activity in recent years is gradually translating into residential project completions, supporting demand for building material products
- Rising demand from solar, EV charging infrastructure pickup and growing electrical-safety awareness are opening growth opportunities in switchgear
- Cable demand is supported by infrastructure expansion, private sector investment, the renewable energy transition, and growth across data centres, railways, metro networks and IT sectors, though copper/aluminium price volatility creates pricing uncertainty
- Continued LED price deflation is a structural headwind weighing on the lighting segment despite festive-led uptick
- Nearly one-third of Havells' revenue accrues from cooling products (air conditioners, fans, air coolers, refrigerators), so a weak/short summer materially affects overall performance
- The government's PM Suryaghar Yojana (target of one crore rooftop solar installations by March 2027) continues to act as a demand driver for the 'others'/solar segment
- India's medium-term outlook is viewed as positive, underpinned by domestic stability and reforms (income tax relief, GST rationalisation, monetary easing) expected to gradually uplift consumer demand and discretionary spending
- Global trade volatility (US tariff actions, geopolitical conflict in West Asia) and a weakening rupee are flagged as near-term uncertainties affecting commodity costs and export performance
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Strong resilient top-line with **calibrated 7–8% price hikes fully passed on**, but reported profitability was deliberately dented by a **>2x YoY jump in advertising spend** (Rs 286 cr, front-loaded into Q1) that management frames as long-term brand investment and expects to normalize. The soft spots are structural-competitive: switchgear (highest-margin segment) hit by West Asia export disruption (−4% sales, −260 bps margin), and cables/wires + Lloyd ACs conceding share to peers on a distribution "sell-in → sell-out" reset. Management (as always) gives **no annual guidance** but signals stabilizing contribution margins, a Rs 1,400 cr FY27 capex, and a strategically scaling renewables business now carved out separately.

Rising raw material prices (copper) in late March/April flagged as a headwind that may require price increases and pressure margins.
New refrigerator plant coming up for Lloyd; refrigerators currently sourced, in-house manufacturing to improve contribution over time.
Lloyd US HVAC product still under development; meaningful traction expected next year (FY26).
Channel inventories (AC/fans/coolers) expected to normalize by end of Q3FY26; distribution channel (>50% of sales) normalized by end Q3, MT/e-com in Q4.
High channel and company inventory in AC/fans/coolers after weak summer; expected to take a few months (into Q2/Q3) to normalize.
